body.estimand_functional: \(\mathsf C(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{sup}},\{X_i^{(m)}:m\in\mathcal E,\ i\le N_r\})=(\widehat{\mathcal G},\widehat H)\in\{(I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I,\widetilde H):\mathcal L_{\mathrm{enc}}(\widetilde H,P)\le\tau\}\cup\{\bot\},\quad r\ge r_0\)

sampling_model.design: A preliminary \(n\)-draw observational support batch is disjoint from the covariance streams and spans the deterministic support \(\mathcal S\) with probability one. Its span determines the canonical frame \(U\). Each environment then supplies one retained post-support stream; stage \(r\) uses exactly its first \(N_r=2^r\) coordinate observations \(Y_i^{(m)}=U^{\top}X_i^{(m)}\), so after stage zero only \(N_r-N_{r-1}\) new observations are appended. Stages before \(r_0=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\) sample only. At each \(r\ge r_0\), error \(\alpha\,2^{-r-1}\) is spent and the public transcript is restarted using the cumulative \(n\times n\) empirical covariances.
sampling_model.units: Independent centered Gaussian observations in each of the \(n+1\) environments, represented in fixed \(n\)-dimensional coordinates on the deterministic common support \(\mathcal S=\operatorname{col}(G)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Environment \(m\in[n]\) is one unknown-target stochastic perfect variance reset; environment \(0\) is observational.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition is used; the relevant regularity is observed-covariance conditioning by \(\kappa\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For \(r\ge r_0\), cumulative \(n\times n\) empirical second moments from exactly \(N_r\) retained coordinate observations are inverted and mapped exactly to Gaussian score-correlation matrices under the induced laws \(P_m\); no inverse is attempted earlier and no learned score nuisance is required.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 5 and Theorem 1 select \(\eta\in(0,\eta^{\ast})\) with equation (22)'s all-subset eigenvalue minimum and \(\gamma\in(0,\gamma^{\ast})\) with equation (23)'s printed minimum norm product, under Assumption 1 and score-difference consistency.
For all non-empty subsets of intervention indices, Lemma 4.3 gives a uniform eigenvalue perturbation bound.
Our work develops confidence sequences whose widths go to zero, with nonasymptotic coverage guarantees under nonparametric conditions.
A single intervention on each latent variable is sufficient for identifiability.
Corollary 4.5 computes an approximate spectral projector within prescribed operator-norm error.

body.tldr: As an exact-real statistical procedure on the declared linear Gaussian variance-reset class, the certificate returns the environment-labelled transitive closure \(I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I\) and an environment-indexed encoder estimate within \(\tau\) of the parent-supported population range class, or abstains. Its per-environment sample bound is quadratic in \(1/\tau\) and essentially linear in \(\log(1/\alpha)\), up to displayed logarithms. Separately, rational post-summary rank, repeated-eigenspace, projector-product, and singular-value decisions admit a proved polynomial-bit implementation with an explicit aggregate rounding budget. The encoder output is neither asserted invertible nor a unique representative of a repeated positive eigenspace. A legal all-dimension Gaussian family has constant reached gaps but exponentially small unqueried equation-(22) margin, showing that the published global margin is not necessary for recoverability, without extending the positive Gaussian theorem to the full published class.

project_justification.gap: Acartürk et al.'s finite-sample graph-recovery premise combines equation (22)'s global all-subset margin \(\eta^{\ast}\), equation (23)'s printed norm-product scale \(\gamma^{\ast}\), Assumption 1, smooth full-support models, distinct interventions, and consistent score estimation. Its rank analysis still pays for every subset although the deterministic program executes only a polynomial transcript, and its printed norm product must not be identified with the reciprocal lower bound furnished by actual projector geometry.
project_justification.niche: A public query-local beta-min contract can separate statistical recoverability from post-selection thresholding while targeting only the graph and encoder class indexed by observed intervention labels.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies an anytime-valid exact-real Gaussian recover-or-abstain certificate with public reached gaps, a sharper cap \(B_{\mathrm{samp}}<66q_{\star}u_{\star}\), environment-labelled graph and encoder targets, and explicit encoder error bars. The resulting per-environment dependence is quadratic in \(1/\tau\) and essentially linear in \(\log(1/\alpha)\), rather than the anchor paper's RKHS fourth-power accuracy dependence. It also supplies a deterministic polynomial-bit post-summary realization with total arithmetic enclosure error at most \(e_{\star}/4\). The positive theorem remains confined to the Gaussian variance-reset subclass; the all-dimension family establishes over the broader published class only that equation \(22\) is not necessary.

body.related_work: Acartürk et al. (2024) are the strict finite-sample comparator. Their Section 5 equation (22) takes a positive-eigenvalue minimum over all subset sums, while printed equation (23) and Lemma 10 identify a projector-product quantity with \(\min_i\|H_{i,:}\|_2\|G_{:,i}\|_2\). The latter norm product is at least one by biorthogonality even though a projector-product norm is at most one, so the present proofs use the actual subspaces and the valid reciprocal witness bound \(\rho_i(G)\), never the printed identity. The positive certificate is a covariance-specialized result for the linear Gaussian perfect variance-reset subclass and is not a strengthening on the source's full smooth soft-intervention class. The explicit Gaussian family is nevertheless legal in that published class and satisfies Assumption 1 and its other non-margin conditions; its recovery with exponentially small off-transcript \(\eta^{\ast}(P)\) shows only that equation (22) is not necessary. The Gaussian rate has quadratic \(1/\tau\) and essentially linear \(\log(1/\alpha)\) dependence, whereas the anchor's RKHS analysis has fourth-power accuracy dependence. Sobczyk (2025), Corollary 4.5 of arXiv version 2, supplies the deterministic certified spectral-projector primitive; the present theorem adapts it to the zero/positive cluster gap, adds exact rational inertia for rank and projector-product singular-value tests, and budgets their composed error along the adaptive transcript. Varıcı et al. (2025) provide the population score-range program, and Squires et al. (2023) validate the legal linear intervention substrate.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The numerical theorem is a post-summary result: it assumes outward rational enclosures of the exact fixed-coordinate empirical covariance summaries and, for a rational ambient encoder, a supplied enclosure of the canonical support frame. Processing raw observations additionally incurs their representation, reading, and covariance-formation cost, including at least \(\Omega(B_{\mathrm{tot}})\) record operations. The statistical theorem remains exact-real at the sampling layer. Its encoder guarantee is distance to a unit-row parent-supported range class, not invertibility, a unique repeated-eigenspace representative, or latent-coordinate error independent of the mixing map. The positive guarantee is specific to Gaussian variance resets and does not transfer to the full published soft-intervention class.
body.honest_scope: The positive statistical and polynomial-bit post-summary theorems concern the linear Gaussian perfect variance-reset subclass in fixed coordinates on \(\mathcal S\). They target only \(I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I\) and the correspondingly environment-indexed parent-supported encoder range class. The rational algorithm is polynomial after covariance summaries are available; an end-to-end raw-data implementation must also pay at least \(\Omega(B_{\mathrm{tot}})\) to read the sample records, so its runtime is not polynomial only in logarithmic gap parameters. The separation family is legal in Acartürk et al.'s broader smooth soft-intervention class and proves that equation (22)'s all-subset margin is not necessary for recovery there, but it does not promote the Gaussian certificate to that broader class. Actual projector geometry and \(\rho_i(G)\) replace the source's false printed norm-product identity. Neither an invertible encoder nor a canonical representative inside a repeated positive eigenspace is claimed.
